Dalmatian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]
Etymology tree
Latin plumbum
Dalmatian plomb

    Inherited from Latin plumbum.

    Noun

    [edit]

    plomb

    1. lead

    References

    [edit]
    • Bartoli, Matteo (1906), Il Dalmatico: Resti di un’antica lingua romanza parlata da Veglia a Ragusa e sua collocazione nella Romània appenino-balcanica, Rome: Istituto della Enciclopedia Italiana, published 2000

    Franco-Provençal

    [edit]

    Alternative forms

    [edit]
    • pllomb (ORB, narrow)

    Etymology

    [edit]
    Etymology tree
    Latin plumbum
    Franco-Provençal plomb

      Inherited from Latin plumbum.

      Noun

      [edit]

      plomb m (plural plombs) (ORB, broad)

      1. lead (metal)

      References

      [edit]
      • plomb in DicoFranPro: Dictionnaire Français/Francoprovençal – on dicofranpro.llm.umontreal.ca
      • plomb in Lo trèsor Arpitan – on arpitan.eu

      French

      [edit]

      Etymology

      [edit]
      Etymology tree
      Latin plumbum
      Old French plom
      Middle French plom
      French plomb

        Inherited from Middle French plom, from Old French plom, from Latin plumbum.

        Pronunciation

        [edit]
        • IPA(key): /plɔ̃/
        • Audio:(file)
        • Audio (France (Toulouse)):(file)
        • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
        • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
        • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
        • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)

        Noun

        [edit]

        plomb m (plural plombs)

        1. lead (metal)
          intoxication saturnine par le plomb ― lead poisoning
        2. fuse
        3. sinker (fishing weight)

        Derived terms

        [edit]
        • avec des pieds de plomb
        • avoir du plomb dans l'aile
        • fil à plomb
        • pétage de plombs
        • péter les plombs
        • péter un plomb
        • plombage
        • plombagine
        • plomber
        • plombier
        • soleil de plomb

        Further reading

        [edit]
        • “plomb”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

          Polish

          [edit]

          Pronunciation

          [edit]
          • IPA(key): /ˈplɔmp/
          • Audio:(file)
          • Rhymes: -ɔmp
          • Syllabification: plomb

          Noun

          [edit]

          Swedish

          [edit]

          Etymology

          [edit]
          Etymology tree
          Latin plumbum
          Old French plom
          Middle French plom
          French plombbor.
          Swedish plomb

            Borrowed from French plomb, from Middle French plom, from Old French plom, from Latin plumbum. Attested since 1829.

            Noun

            [edit]

            plomb c

            1. a (lead) seal (to seal a package)
            2. (dentistry) a filling
            3. (chiefly historical) a filling of concrete in a tree (due to the historical practice of cavity filling)

            Declension

            [edit]
            Declension of plomb
            nominative genitive
            singular indefinite plomb plombs
            definite plomben plombens
            plural indefinite plomber plombers
            definite plomberna plombernas

            Related terms

            [edit]
            • plombera
